data.title: Bihar signs MoUs worth ₹1.72 trillion for nuclear, pumped storage projects
data.description:
The government of Bihar on Friday signed five memoranda of understanding (MoUs) worth ₹1.72 lakh crore with companies for setting up six large energy projects, including two nuclear power plants and four pumped storage projects in the state.
 
The two nuclear power plants will be established in Banka and Siwan districts, while the four pumped storage (PSP) projects will be developed in Nawada, Jamui and Aurangabad districts. The state's Energy and Industries departments had received total investment proposals worth ₹2.25 lakh crore from companies.
 
The MoUs were signed at a ceremony held in Patna in the presence of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, and Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh.
 
 
The event was also attended by Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Energy Secretary-cum-Chairman and Managing Director of Bihar State Power Holding Company (BSPHCL) Ajay Yadav, and Secretary to the Chief Minister Sanjay Kumar Singh.
 
Speaking at the event, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said the agreements had been signed keeping in mind the rising demand for electricity and the pace of industrial development, and the state government aimed to ensure round-the-clock availability of affordable, quality and uninterrupted power to industries by 2030. Referring to the agreements for 11,600 MW of power generation capacity, he said the projects would play an important role in accelerating industrial development and investment.
 
Power generator NTPC signed an MoU for establishing a nuclear power plant with 2,800 megawatt (MW) capacity at Bhitiya in Banka district at a cost of ₹70,000 crore. The project will be developed over 1,500 acres of land and will require an annual water supply of 160 million cubic metres.
 
Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCIL) signed an MoU for setting up a nuclear power plant of 2,800 MW capacity at Talhar, Raghunathpur, in Siwan district at a cost of ₹70,000 crore. The project will be developed over 1,500 acres of land and will require an annual water supply of 160 million cubic metres (MCM).
 
Adani signed two MoUs for setting up two PSP projects of 1,800 MW capacity each, requiring an investment of ₹9,900 crore each. The projects would have an energy storage capacity of 10,800 MWh each and come up in Nawada and Jamui districts.
 
Further, Torrent Energy Storage Solutions would set up a 1,500 MW PSP project at Hardiya/Fulwaria Dam in Nawada district at a cost of ₹7,685 crore. Also, Greenko Energies signed an MoU for investing ₹5,400 crore to set up a PSP project of 900 MW capacity in Aurangabad district.

data.title: Mahindra Last Mile bets on domestic battery cells to improve EV economics
data.description:
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Ltd (MLMML), the small commercial vehicle arm of Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M), is banking on domestic battery cell manufacturing coming onstream over the next two years to deepen localisation, reduce import dependence and improve the economics of its electric vehicle (EV) business.
 
While the company has achieved localisation levels of around 70-75 per cent and assembles its own battery packs, it remains dependent on imported cells, exposing it to global supply-chain disruptions and currency fluctuations.
 
Suman Mishra, managing director and chief executive officer of MLMML, told Business Standard that the EV ecosystem was becoming increasingly resilient through localisation and a sustained government push. The company, she said, had also built a robust supply chain to mitigate shortages.
 
 
“We expect domestic cell manufacturing to come online over the next couple of years as investments by major battery makers translate into production capacity. That will strengthen supply-chain resilience, improve localisation levels and further enhance the economics of electric mobility in India,” Mishra said.
 
The availability of locally manufactured cells assumes significance as EVs account for a growing share of MLMML’s business. Mishra, however, did not specify any domestic cell sourcing arrangements or quantify the potential impact of localisation on margins.
 
Domestic sales of its electric three- and four-wheelers rose 41 per cent year-on-year to 45,287 units in the second quarter of FY27, accounting for nearly 86 per cent of its overall domestic volumes. The company’s share of the electric three-wheeler market stood at 36.2 per cent, according to M&M’s latest investor presentation.
 
Expanding overseas footprint
 
MLMML is looking to tap overseas demand for electric three-wheelers, particularly in Southeast Asia and Africa, even as it works on augmenting manufacturing capacity in India.
 
The company, which already has a presence in Sri Lanka and Nepal, has recently entered the Philippines and is witnessing a surge in export enquiries following its Earthshot Prize win.
 
“Post the Earthshot recognition, we are being inundated with requests from other countries to export our EVs there. We are taking a pragmatic approach and will announce our next international destination soon,” Mishra said.
 
In the near term, the company will cater to international markets from its existing manufacturing facilities at Zaheerabad, Bengaluru and Haridwar, with all exports currently through the completely built-up (CBU) route.
 
MLMML is scouting multiple locations for capacity expansion and is in discussions over the proposed facility. Mishra said setting up a new plant typically takes 12-18 months, adding that existing facilities were well positioned to support near-term export growth.
 
The company will also deploy its £1 million Earthshot Prize grant towards training women drivers, facilitating affordable financing and expanding charging infrastructure in underserved areas.
 
IPO contingent on profitability, capital needs
 
Despite its expansion ambitions, the ₹10,822 crore-valued company, backed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and India Japan Fund, is in no hurry to tap the capital markets.
 
In August, Mishra had indicated a possible initial public offering (IPO) in 12-18 months. She now expects a decision to hinge on sustained growth, improving profitability and the requirement for fresh capital. The company has not disclosed whether it has appointed investment bankers.
 
“Eighteen months is what we are looking at and if we are ready by then, we should do it. We will not be rushing into a listing as we can always rely on the Mahindra Group to fund expansion,” Mishra said.

data.title: Polycab India faces near-term volume, margin pressure as metal prices fall
data.description:
The stock of the country’s largest cable and wires (C&W) company, Polycab India, slipped about 8 per cent over the past week on worries that inventory losses, price cuts and increased competitive pressures will weigh on near-term outlook.
 
While the company delivered a strong September quarter performance, short-term headwinds, a higher year-ago base and peaking growth concerns are likely to lead to growth moderation.
 
After a strong growth trend over the last four years, Polycab may underperform peers, going ahead. At the current price (₹7,575), the stock is trading at about 30 times its FY28 earnings estimates.
 
The sharp correction in copper and aluminium prices and subsequent inventory losses are expected to weigh on the company and the segment.
 
Copper prices at the London Metal Exchange have declined by 11-12 per cent from September highs of $14,870 per metric tonne while aluminum prices have retreated to levels last seen in January 2026.
 
Current spot prices are down 9 per cent for aluminium and 4 per cent for copper and this is below their respective Q2FY27 averages.
 
The 21 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) increase in copper prices in Q3FY26 had prompted distributors to advance purchases ahead of further price hikes.
 
This resulted in unusually strong volume rise during the quarter, with Polycab India registering 40 per cent growth. Also, RR Kabel gained 30 per cent in the domestic market and Finolex Cables surged 28 per cent in the wire business.
 
With metal prices now easing, Nishant Bagrecha and Rohan Kalle of InCred Research believe that distributors could delay replenishment in anticipation of lower procurement costs.
 
If the downtrend persists, channel stocking is likely to remain subdued in Q3FY27.
 
The brokerage has an ‘add’ rating on Polycab with a target price of ₹9,800.
 
Given the disruption in prices and competitive pressures, brokerages expect margins to come under pressure.
 
Overall, operating profit margins in the September quarter for Polycab were down 139 basis points (bps) year-on-year (Y-o-Y) while it improved by 53 bps on a sequential basis.
 
While margins in the core C&W segment was at 14.2 per cent, profitability in the fast moving electrical goods (FMEG) segment stood at its highest level of 10.1 per cent.
 
The financial health of the FMEG segment has been improving and the business reported its seventh consecutive profitable quarter.
 
While there is price volatility once commodity prices stabilise, margins are expected to recover given volume uptick and operating leverage.
 
Motilal Oswal Research also points out that the C&W segment is entering a more challenging phase amid several headwinds such as a sharp correction in copper/aluminum prices. This typically triggers inventory losses as well as faster price pass-through and channel de-stocking.
 
The other risks — according to the brokerage — are the increase in competitive intensity with the entry of UltraTech Cement (Ultravolt brand) and uncertainty around global artificial intelligence (AI)/data centre-led infrastructure spending.
 
Growth momentum for the segment is expected to moderate in the near term due to the recent softness in commodity prices. This follows a strong 18 per cent value growth delivered by organised players over the FY22-26 period.
 
Sanjeev Kumar Singh and Mudit Agarwal of the brokerage point out that multiple headwinds led the Polycab stock to derate from its peak valuation of 40-42 times price-to-earnings (PE) on a one-year forward basis to about 30 times.
 
They, however, maintain a ‘buy’ rating on the stock with a target price of ₹10,000.
 
Their ‘buy’ call is based on its leadership position in the C&W industry and a strong balance sheet which supports business operations during volatile market conditions.

data.title: SC declines to revive CCI probe against Star India, Sony Pictures Network
data.description:
The Supreme Court has refused to revive a Competition Commission of India (CCI) investigation into alleged anti-competitive practices by Star India Private Limited and Sony Pictures Network India Private Limited in the television broadcasting industry.
 
A Bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed the CCI's challenge to a 2019 Bombay High Court judgment that had quashed the regulator's orders directing an investigation into allegations of discriminatory business practices by the two broadcasters.
 
The Bench took note of the fact that the CCI's special leave petition had remained pending for nearly six years without even being taken up for admission. It questioned why the commission had failed to secure an early hearing during this period.
 
 
The court observed that the challenge related to a 2019 order and that no effective steps appeared to have been taken to ensure its timely listing.
 
"It has been six years. You have not even got notice issued in the matter," Justice Pardiwala remarked.
 
The Bench also asked the CCI what efforts it had made during the intervening years to have the petition listed for admission.
 
Appearing for the commission, its counsel submitted that applications seeking an early hearing had been filed in 2020 and 2022. The matter had also been mentioned before the Supreme Court Registry in 2022, counsel said, adding that documents substantiating these steps could be placed before the court.
 
The counsel attributed the delay to issues concerning the listing and allocation of the matter before different Benches and urged the court to consider the attempts made to secure an early hearing.
 
The Bench, however, remained unconvinced, pointing out that the petition had not progressed even to the admission stage despite having been filed several years ago.
 
The dispute originated from a complaint filed by Noida Software Technology Park Limited (NSTPL), a television channel distributor, against Star India and Sony Pictures.
 
NSTPL alleged that the broadcasters had denied it fair and non-discriminatory access to their channels while extending preferential commercial terms to competing distribution platform operators.
 
The distributor had entered into interconnection agreements with content aggregators distributing Star and Sony channels. It alleged that the broadcasters offered preferential rates and discounts to other operators but imposed discriminatory commercial conditions on it.
 
On June 7, 2017, NSTPL approached the CCI, alleging violations of Sections 3 and 4 of the Competition Act, 2002.
 
Following the complaint, the commission passed orders on July 27 and July 31, 2018, directing its Director General to investigate the alleged discriminatory refusal to deal by the broadcasters.
 
Star India and Sony Pictures challenged these directions before the Bombay High Court.
 
In its October 16, 2019, judgment, the High Court set aside the CCI's orders and the consequential proceedings initiated by the regulator.
 
The High Court held that the commission had not established a prima facie case of an agreement involving refusal to deal that could adversely affect competition. It also found that the CCI had failed to examine the relevant factors prescribed under Section 19(3) of the Competition Act before ordering an investigation.
 
The CCI subsequently approached the Supreme Court, challenging the High Court's decision.

data.title: OM: Operation Mole box office Day 1: Dhanush-Mammootty film starts strong
data.description:
Dhanush and Mammootty's much-awaited OM: Operation Mole has finally been released in theatres. The action thriller arrived today, on Friday, November 20, amid major expectations from movie lovers. Directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, the film stars Sai Pallavi and Sreeleela. 
 
According to Sacnilk, the film earned ₹8.7 crore net in India by 4 pm. Its domestic gross collection was ₹10.80 crore during the same time. The final opening-day figures can be expected later tonight.

Om advance booking report 

As per Sacnilk, the film projected an opening of ₹17-20 crore gross in India. It is expected that OM's worldwide collections could reach ₹25-30 crore, potentially surpassing Dhanush’s 50th film, Raayan's ₹22.97 crore debut, according to Sacnilk.
 

OM Operation Mole Day 1 box office update

The film recorded its strongest initial run from Tamil-speaking viewers. Its Tamil version earned ₹5.16 crore net across 2,082 shows. This accounted for a gross of around 78.1% of the total collection. Meanwhile, the Telugu version earned ₹1.34 crore across 751 shows. The Hindi version collected ₹11 lakh across 368 shows. 
 
Sacnilk tracked 3,201 shows across the 3 languages. The figures show Tamil audiences are driving the film's opening-day business. However, these numbers represent only the early collections. Evening and night shows could majorly influence the final box office collection. Also Read: OTT releases this week: List of new OTTs to watch on various platforms
 

About OM Operation Mole 

The movie brings together Dhanush and Malayalam superstar Mammootty in a major collaboration. Rajkumar Periasamy has written and directed this big project. The story tells of a violent world where criminals and law-enforcement officers operate in close proximity. 
 
Greed, power and poverty shape the battles unfolding between its roles. The supporting cast includes Naseeruddin Shah, Renu Desai and Indrans. The film's duration is 2 hours and 58 minutes. Its theatrical release covers Tamil, Telugu and Hindi audiences.

data.title: Rail link, trading post, infra projects on anvil during Nepal PM visit
data.description:
During Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s two-day visit to New Delhi, which begins on Sunday, India is likely to announce a substantial economic package for its northern neighbour. Agreements are also slated to be inked between the two sides on investments in Nepal's education, health and hydropower sectors and to increase connectivity, including reciprocal overflight access.
 
A $2 billion development package from India, some of which will help with reconstruction projects in Nepal following the glacial floods in August, is being discussed. Sources said the two sides are still giving final shape to the package. If finalised, it will be the largest such one-time package that India has given to any of its neighbours. The glacial flood in Nepal left over 1,500 people dead, with over 5,200 still missing, and damaged over 7,000 homes and several hydroelectric projects.
 
 
A cross-border weekly train service connecting Nepal’s Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantonment will be flagged off, and an integrated check post in the border town of Banbasa in Uttarakhand’s Champawat district, 50 km from Uttar Pradesh’s Pilibhit district, will be inaugurated.
 
The Nepal PM will land in New Delhi on Sunday afternoon and hold delegation-level talks with Modi on Monday, leaving for Kathmandu a little after that. This will be Shah’s first bilateral visit not just to India but outside Nepal since forming his government after his party, the Rastriya Swatantra Party, won a landslide in the general elections. He travelled to New York in September to address the United Nations General Assembly.
 
Modi and Shah will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement it issued on Friday afternoon. It said India-Nepal bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress in trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports.
 
In Kathmandu on Friday, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said a 34-member delegation comprising Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Minister of Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal and others will accompany Shah to New Delhi. Wagle was in India for a three-day visit in September and also visited in October, while India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri was in Kathmandu earlier this month. Both India and Nepal have appointed new ambassadors to each other’s capitals. A 52-member business delegation from Nepal will also be in India during the Nepal PM’s visit to New Delhi, and a Nepal-India Business Forum is slated to meet.

data.title: OTT releases this week: List of new OTTs to watch on various platforms
data.description:
Are you searching for a new OTT series for your weekend watch? This week has seen a variety of films and web series debut on OTT platforms, showcasing a blend of genres including comedy, romance, drama, thrillers, and action. 
 
Highlighted by the highly anticipated film The Odyssey from Christopher Nolan and the return of the beloved comedy series Dhindora featuring Bhuvan Bam in its second season, there is a lot to consider for your watchlist.

data.title: Industry body GJC alerts BIS over gold adulteration using Rhenium, Iridium
data.description:
The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) on Friday said it alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) about reports of the alleged use of Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys to increase gold's weight, and urged the industry and consumers to remain vigilant.

"While there have been media reports from certain quarters regarding the possible misuse of materials such as Rhenium and Iridium in gold, we want to assure the entire jewellery industry and all gold buyers that there is absolutely no reason to panic. The Bureau of Indian Standards is treating the matter with utmost seriousness," GJC Chairman Rajesh Rokde said in a statement.

 

According to media reports, Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys were allegedly used to increase gold's weight without a corresponding increase in purity.

GJC appealed to all jewellers and consumers to immediately report any instance of suspected adulteration, fraudulent activity or malpractice.

"Such complaints can be lodged with GJC as well as directly with the Bureau of Indian Standards, enabling prompt investigation and necessary action," Rokde said.

He said every jeweller must undertake stringent quality control checks of gold procured from manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers and keep consumer service as the top priority.

He advised buyers not to fall prey to lower making charge offers and to purchase gold only from trusted retailers.

Consumers should also verify hallmark details through the BIS Care App and insist on GST-paid invoices, said Rokde.

"We remain committed to protecting the interests of both the industry and consumers. Any proven case of adulteration or malpractice will be strongly pursued with the appropriate authorities, and strict action should be taken against anyone found manufacturing, supplying or using such materials for fraudulent purposes," he said.

GJC Vice Chairman Avinash Gupta said isolated reports or rumours should not be allowed to undermine consumer confidence in the gems and jewellery sector.

"We encourage all jewellers to strengthen internal quality control processes and ensure complete compliance and transparency with BIS hallmarking regulations. Consumers, on their part, should purchase jewellery only from reputable jewellers, obtain proper invoices and verify hallmark credentials before making a purchase," he added.

data.title: Machine tool makers seek ₹3,000 crore fund to cut dependence on imports
data.description:
The Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers’ Association (IMTMA) has sought a ₹3,000-crore government-backed fund to acquire 25-30 advanced manufacturing technologies from Europe and the United States, aiming to reduce the country’s dependence on imported machine tools by ₹8,000-10,000 crore.
 
The proposal is part of the industry’s recommendations for the Union Budget 2027-28, which the association plans to raise with the Secretary of the Ministry of Heavy Industries on Saturday.
 
The proposed Machine Tool Technology Acquisition Fund would comprise ₹1,000 crore in grants, ₹1,000 crore in soft loans and another ₹1,000 crore for equity co-investment by the government in strategic transactions, according to the association’s detailed note on Budget demands.
  
The association said India continues to import 60 per cent of its metalworking machine tools by value, with high-end technologies concentrated in Europe and the US. It argued that high interest rates in India make overseas technology acquisitions prohibitively expensive for domestic manufacturers.
 
The industry demands come at a time when domestic consumption of machine tools has outpaced domestic production. This “widening gap between demand and supply is being filled by rising imports,” said Mohini Kelkar, president of IMTMA. According to the association, the value of machine tool production increased by 19 per cent year-on-year to ₹17,387 crore in FY26, against a 15 per cent rise in domestic consumption to ₹36,419 crore. Imports, meanwhile, grew 16 per cent year-on-year to ₹21,628 crore during the same period. “China accounts for almost 25 per cent of such imports,” Kelkar said, adding that a lack of technology is the biggest impediment to domestic production.
 
The association has also sought a separate ₹1,000-crore technology upgradation fund to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It has proposed an interest subsidy of 5-6 per cent, with assistance capped at ₹200 crore per enterprise, a loan tenure of seven to 10 years and a two-year moratorium.
 
IMTMA said Indian machine tool MSMEs currently pay interest rates of around 7-10 per cent on loans for technology upgradation, compared with subsidised rates of 1-4 per cent in China, 2-4 per cent in South Korea and 1-3 per cent in Taiwan.
 
Separately, the association has called for a dedicated production-linked incentive (PLI)-like scheme to promote the indigenisation of core machine tool technologies. The industry has sought a requirement for companies benefiting from PLI schemes to source at least 60 per cent of their overall capital goods procurement from domestic manufacturers.
 
IMTMA has also proposed setting up a National Mission for Core Technologies, jointly anchored by a national research and development institution, academia and the machine tool industry.
 
On the trade policy front, the association has sought an additional 2 per cent basic customs duty on imports under the broad ‘Others’ classification of machinery and mechanical appliances under HS Code 84798999. It said imports under this category stood at $2.19 billion in 2025-26, arguing that the classification could be used to import machinery without adequate product-specific identification. The proposed duty would apply even to imports under free and preferential trade agreements.
 
The industry has also sought access to granular, machine-wise import data to identify the types, specifications and sources of imported machinery, including a distinction between new and second-hand equipment. It has urged the government to reconsider Section 135AA of the Customs Act, which it says has restricted access to such information, or alternatively allow relevant ministries to access the data for policy planning and import substitution.
 
The association has further sought discontinuation of the Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) scheme, or its restriction to machinery that is not manufactured domestically. It argued that zero-duty imports under the scheme create a cost disadvantage for Indian capital goods manufacturers, which pay duties on imported components and taxes on domestic procurement.

data.title: DFS Secy urges banks, NBFCs to collaborate on cyber security amid AI risks
data.description:
Banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and insurers need to collaborate and share their cyber defence strategies rather than treat them as proprietary information, Sanjay Lohiya, Secretary, Department of Financial Services (DFS), said on Thursday, flagging cyber security and financial fraud as among the biggest challenges facing the financial sector.
 
With incidents of bank fraud, data breaches and cyber attacks becoming increasingly frequent, he called on financial institutions to strengthen their cyber security infrastructure and avoid compromising on the quality of software, protocols and manpower.
 
Speaking at the CII-DFS Financing Summit, Lohiya said, “Now, not a week goes when we do not hear any incident of a bank having defrauded few crore of rupees or some data having been exposed or some NBFC has had data compromise or money transferred.”
 
 
He said financial institutions needed to recognise cyber security as a collective challenge, with greater sharing of information and defence strategies helping the sector respond better to emerging threats.
 
“Instead of various banks and NBFCs or insurance companies treating such whatever work they are doing towards protecting their own data or their funds, etc, as a proprietary item or some trade secret, instead if we share strategies with each other, it will help us to all build this safety against such frauds,” Lohiya said.
 
He also flagged the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) in cyber attacks, although he said the extent to which such attacks had been established was not entirely clear.
 
“It is a new beast so to say and we all have to put our heads together and all institutions whether small or big, they have to pay full attention to this part about cyber security,” he said.
 
Lohiya said institutions should not compromise on the quality of their cyber security products, protocols, software or personnel. He called for greater interaction among banks, technology vendors and solution providers to help financial institutions adopt available safeguards.
 
He said he had asked the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) to initiate regular interactions among banks and technology vendors on cyber security measures. He also urged CII to take the discussion forward and facilitate greater cooperation among financial sector participants.
 
The growing threat of cyber fraud comes amid a significant expansion in the scale and scope of the banking and financial services sector over the past decade, driven by the growth of digital payments, fintech companies, NBFCs and financial products. Lohiya said the sector would need to strengthen its capabilities to meet emerging challenges as it plays a crucial role in financing the government's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.
 
Lohiya said the high-level committee on banking for Viksit Bharat, announced in the Union Budget, had begun its work and was examining the legislative and regulatory changes required in the sector, along with a roadmap for the financial system.
 
“Towards that effort, already the committee has circulated questionnaires to some of the stakeholders and they will be taking in-person discussions with the stakeholders. The committee will be here in Mumbai on 2nd and 3rd (of December), next to next week, in Mumbai to listen to the stakeholders here and they will be also holding meetings in Delhi and maybe some other places,” he said.
 
He urged industry participants to submit their suggestions and engage with the committee as it examines the sector's requirements. He said the government and regulators were open to suggestions on addressing the challenges facing the financial sector.
 
On financial inclusion, Lohiya said efforts needed to move beyond opening bank accounts towards making credit easily accessible, particularly to the poorest sections of society.
 
While initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana had helped expand access to banking, the next challenge was to ensure that account holders could access credit and undertake financial transactions. Schemes such as Mudra and microfinance had helped address this need, but banks and other financial institutions needed to make greater efforts to reach borrowers at the bottom of the pyramid, he said.
 
MSME financing was another area that required attention, Lohiya said, noting that several initiatives were being undertaken by the Ministry of MSME, the finance ministry, banks and NBFCs. Platforms such as the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) were expanding their scope, with efforts underway to make them more widely accessible.
 
He also flagged a shift in the housing market over the past five to 10 years. While affordable housing had earlier accounted for a large share of new launches, the market had increasingly shifted towards the higher-end segment.
 
“A lot of housing market has now become what they call is a luxury segment. So, there is a real shortage of, I would say, affordable housing,” he said, adding that mass housing was a key requirement and banks, NBFCs and other financial institutions had an important role to play in financing it.
 
Lohiya also said insurance companies, pension funds and corporate bond markets could play an important role in meeting the country's financing requirements. While the government and regulators had taken several steps in this direction, further measures might be needed. However, he cautioned that investors providing patient capital should not be exposed to unexpected risks.
 
He said the government and regulators were open to suggestions from industry on addressing the sector's challenges, adding that greater collaboration between policymakers and financial institutions would be crucial to strengthening the sector's contribution to the country's development goals.
